questions.text:

element memory[20]; // Global memory declaration
int top[4];
int boundary[4];

i) Write the C code snippet required to initialize the top and boundary of each stack.

questions.reason: Implementing four stacks requires a consistent shared-array partition scheme across initialization, push and pop, with distinct empty and full bounds for every stack, including the last partition. This is a complete adaptation of a stack implementation with several coupled index invariants, rather than one supplied push/pop operation. Fixed partitions suffice; dynamic space sharing is not required, so Hard is not justified.

questions.text:
You are provided with the array representation of a binary tree.

questions.text:
A small delivery network is represented as an undirected graph. The network has six hubs labelled A, B, C, D, E, F. The direct connections between hubs are: A-B, A-C, B-D, C-E, D-F, E-F, B-C, D-E Note: Whenever there is a choice between multiple unvisited neighbours in DFS or BFS, hubs should be selected in alphabetical order.
i. If a delivery inspection follows Depth First Search (DFS) starting from hub A, which hub will be inspected last? Explain your reasoning.
ii. If a delivery inspection follows Breadth First Search (BFS) starting from hub A, which hub is the farthest from A in terms of the number of connections?
iii. Determine the number of connected subnetworks in this network.
Now, remove the link E-F and D-F from the network. How many connected subnetworks exist after these removals?
iv. If all connections become one-way (directed) in the order: A→ B→ D→F, A→C→E→F, B→C, D→ E, can DFS starting from A reach all hubs? Provide a brief explanation.
v. Which change in the underlying data structure (queue ↔ stack) would make BFS behave like

DFS?
questions.reason: Several short traces on a 6-vertex graph: DFS order (A,B,C,E,D,F, so F is last), BFS distance (F farthest at 3 edges), component count (1, and still 1 after removals with F isolated? No: removing E-F and D-F isolates F, giving 2), directed reachability (yes), and the queue-to-stack swap. DFS is the first substantive task; BFS, components and reachability are secondary. Pure hand simulation. #547 and #1971 implement these ideas but are not needed for a trace.
